metrics.name: mc_economy_flow_total
metrics.help: Amounts moved, as absolute values. direction = in|out. The ratio of the two tells whether the economy is creating or destroying currency.

metrics.name: mc_economy_player_balance
metrics.help: Balance of an online player. Updated by event, so accurate to the second — no database reads.

collector.name: economy
collector.text:
ExcellentEconomy's multi-currency economy — by events, and by REFLECTION. COMPLEMENTS the `essentials` module, which gives the TOTAL in circulation by reading EssentialsX's already-computed cache. This one gives the MOVEMENT: who earns, who spends, how much, in which currency. A total that doesn't move and a heavy flow don't describe the same economy, and neither metric replaces the other. WHY REFLECTION HERE, AND NOWHERE ELSE. ExcellentEconomy is compiled as **class 69, i.e. Java 25** — verified in its jar. A javac targeting Java 21 refuses to READ such a file, even for a plain signature: 
 bad class file: ExcellentEconomy-2.8.0.jar(…/ChangeBalanceEvent.class) class file has wrong version 69.0, should be 65.0
The two clean options were compiling this module with `--release 25`, which forces a JDK 25 to build the whole repo, or dropping it. Reflection is the third path: the module stays compilable on the repo's JDK 21, and `registerEvent` accepts a class obtained at runtime. The cost is that a signature change on NightExpress's side won't show up at compile time — it will show up at startup, as a warning, and the module will stay silent instead of failing to build.
